newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell nickel stake by mid-December.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell nickel stake by mid-December.

text.p: Colombia will sell its minority stake in Cerro Matoso S.A., one of the world's largest nickel producers, by mid-December, Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Thursday.
"We expect to approve the sale of Cerro Matoso at a cabinet meeting on Monday, September 16," Ocampo told Reuters.

"The sale will be completed by no later than mid-December," he added, saying South Africa's Gencor Ltd, which owns a 52.3 percent interest in the mine, was among possible buyers of the government's 47.7 percent stake.
Ocampo did not elaborate, but he said the government expected to receive more than $100 million from the privatization.
Energy and Mines Minister Rodrigo Villamizar recently estimated annual nickel production from the mine at 65 million pounds, up from 53 million pounds two years ago.

Villamizar said the mine, the world's fourth largest, could easily produce upwards of 80 million pounds of nickel a year but that it would require the building of additional furnace to collect the metal from residuals.
Gencor has put plans to build another furnace on hold until it sees whether its concession to operate the mine will be extended beyond the year 2005.
Ocampo said the concession terms were one of the issues that would be dicussed at the cabinet meeting later this month.
